title: Introduction to Neural Alignment and Dynamic Programming

transcript.text: Welcome everyone. Today we are discussing sequence alignment algorithms in computational biology and speech.
As you can see on slide one, sequence alignment finds the optimal correspondence between two time series.
Now, pay attention because this is NOT on the slides: in next week's midterm, remember that dynamic time warping requires a strictly monotonic step constraint to prevent temporal loops!
Moving to slide two, here is the dynamic programming recurrence relation for global sequence alignment.
Notice that the time complexity is order O(N times M). Professor's verbal tip: for very long lectures, you should use banded diagonal search to cut runtime by 70 percent.
That concludes our overview. Please review the practice problems before our next session.
